hero.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Fourth of July with Fireworks and America 250 Events Today
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida advances rules barring undocumented students from state colleges and adult education programs
cards.body:
Florida's State Board of Education voted to move forward with rules that would prevent undocumented students from enrolling in the state's 28 community colleges and adult education programs. The restrictions would also affect GED preparation courses, which many students use as a pathway to college or workforce training. This action follows a similar decision by Florida's public university system, which approved a plan to bar undocumented students starting in the 2027-28 academic year. Students already enrolled would not be affected by the university proposal.

Those backing the restrictions argue that taxpayer-funded educational institutions should prioritize students who are legally present in the United States. However, immigrant advocates and students have strongly opposed the changes. Alexander Vallejos, a student with DACA protections, argued that the rules would shut doors for young people raised in Florida who graduated from Florida schools. "We're just asking for an opportunity to earn our future through education," Vallejos said. "Because when Dreamers succeed, Florida succeeds." These new restrictions build on Florida's earlier decision to eliminate in-state tuition rates for many undocumented students, including those protected under DACA.

The education restrictions are part of a broader week of political activity in Florida under Governor Ron DeSantis. The governor moved to use a new state law, effective July 1, that allows the state to designate organizations as terrorist groups. DeSantis announced that Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood, and Antifa as terrorist organizations, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations including cartel-connected groups and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. If approved by the Cabinet, these designations could cut off taxpayer funding, government contracts, and other public support to listed groups and create penalties for providing material support.

CAIR and civil rights organizations immediately filed lawsuits in federal court, arguing that the designations violate constitutional protections. Scott McCoy, deputy legal director for the Southern Poverty Law Center, stated that "Gov. DeSantis does not have the power to unilaterally brand an organization with this vilifying designation and punish those who support it without due process or judicial review." The lawsuit contends the designation process infringes on free speech and due process rights. DeSantis and supporters of the law maintain that the state is taking necessary steps to combat extremism and protect public institutions.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher sus.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back. It's unclear when a final decision will be made.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds raises $90 million as GOP governor's race heats up with ballot eligibility lawsuit
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds entered the week with more than $90 million raised this cycle as Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed a lawsuit challenging another candidate's ballot eligibility.
cards.body:
Byron Donalds and his affiliated political committee have raised more than $90 million this cycle, including more than $23 million in the second quarter. The campaign launched a $20 million statewide advertising buy as Florida's August primary draws closer. Donalds picked up endorsements from Attorney General James Uthmeier and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, both appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis, plus backing from incoming Senate President Jim Boyd and House Speaker Sam Garrison. DeSantis himself has not endorsed a successor in the race to replace him as he faces term limits, though several figures connected to his administration have begun lining up behind Donalds.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed a lawsuit arguing that Republican candidate James Fishback does not meet Florida's constitutional requirement that a governor live in the state for at least seven years before being elected. The legal complaint points to Fishback's ties to Washington, D.C., including allegations that he claimed a D.C. property as a primary residence and voted there in 2020. Fishback denied the allegations, arguing he was born and raised in Florida and accusing Collins of trying to damage his campaign. Fishback suggested without providing evidence that Collins is working in concert with Donalds. The court fight adds uncertainty to the GOP primary, with mail ballots going out soon and the Aug. 18 primary approaching.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby for Fourth of July weekend boaters
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit teams are deploying two boats with medics to the north and south areas of the county as hundreds of boaters take to the wat.
cards.body:
Martin County Maritime Response Unit is preparing for a surge of holiday boaters this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry said his team will deploy two boats with medics stationed in the north and south areas of the county to respond to emergencies. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, prioritizing safety on the water. Lt. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said as maritime response teams remain on standby throughout the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for hundreds of Fourth of July boaters
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is placing two boats with medics on standby for the Fourth of July weekend as hundreds of boaters take to the waterways.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit the waterways across Florida this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team anticipates the busy holiday celebration on the water. The unit will have two boats with medics on standby positioned in both north and south Martin County to respond to emergencies.

Harry said the Maritime Response Unit is prepared to assist boaters with any situation, from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious medical emergencies including cardiac issues or potential spinal injuries. Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy, are prioritizing safety during their holiday outings. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lt. Gov. Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous social media accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts were deactivated after allegations tied them to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, with accusations coming from prominent veterans of Gov. Ron DeSantis' communications team.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, identified two X accounts they alleged were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to a known number and email used by Layla Collins. Screenshots verified this through two-factor authentication, displaying a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits visible.

Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. After Pushaw and Redfern publicly leveled these criticisms, both accounts were deactivated. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents push for new fence at JB-7 beach access after removal sparks trespassing disputes
hero.teaser: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers have been cutting through private property since the town removed a fence at the JB-7 public beach walkway in 2023. The Juno Beach Town Council will take up the fence question during budget discussions on July 15.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach are experiencing increased trespassing problems since the town removed a fence from the JB-7 public beach access point in 2023. The fence was taken down for safety reasons, but its absence has left only bushes to mark the boundary between the public walkway and private property. During peak summer months, Colony residents report that beachgoers regularly park in private parking spots and cut through landscaping to access the beach, carrying coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs across what should be private land.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the situation has become a frequent source of conflict. She noted that residents previously tried confronting trespassers directly but found that approach unsuccessful. "We used to confront them and tell them this is private property, and they would get pretty rude. So, now what we've just been doing is just calling the police, and they've been coming up and confronting them," Hill said. The recurring incidents have prompted residents to seek a permanent solution that would restore the clear property boundary a fence once provided.

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting. Town officials stated that the municipality is not obligated to install a fence on the property. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern indicated openness to exploring lower-cost alternatives. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The council decided to include the fence question in its budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

Not everyone views the situation as problematic. Michael House, a beachgoer who frequents the area, said he has not observed the trespassing issues described by residents and noted that ample free parking is available nearby. However, residents remain hopeful that the town will address their concerns. "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking," Hill said. The council's upcoming budget meeting will determine whether the town moves forward with installing new fencing or pursuing an alternative solution to resolve the ongoing dispute between residents and beach visitors.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The National Civic League selected Riviera Beach as one of just 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award. The city was the only Florida winner this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, stating that Riviera Beach earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize the community and improve quality of life for residents. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents and that winning reinforces the city's positive momentum.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment. These include the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Miller-Anderson said winning the award brings back community pride and represents the city's broader commitment to treating civic engagement as an ongoing partnership between government, residents, faith groups, schools and community organizations.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County School District earns third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. The district set a record graduation rate of 93.5%.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County received an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. The Florida Department of Education assigns letter grades based on student performance on state tests, graduation rates and student performance on advanced coursework. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, earned "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record graduation rate of 93.5%, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the district's most dramatic success stories came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which jumped from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years in the principal role and five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround by modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program three years ago, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Three other district schools also improved from "C" to "A" ratings: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year as ground beef and strawberry prices climb
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%.
cards.body:
A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, while buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%, and ice cream prices have increased 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting those planning to serve potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommended shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals on groceries. Woroch emphasized that reducing food waste is crucial for families, and said that process begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction hours before surgery at Treasure Coast facility
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery at a Treasure Coast facility, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that is popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week later, thanks to her plastic surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington. Billington uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and argues the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Anthem responded to the denial by stating the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval, though the company noted it covers alternative evidence-based options. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction following reporting on patient denials. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march at Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m. The band will march a full mile along the National Mall from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the moment, saying "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching. It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion." She explained the physical demands of marching band, noting that performers must "play, you have to breathe, you have to walk" while maintaining consistent sound.

Senior Stephin Restivo emphasized the team's focus on execution, stating the band is "just focusing on the marching, the timing of everything. Everybody is going to be able to see it. Everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying "I have full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those unable to attend in person.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community rallies to support fiance
hero.teaser: Friends launched a fundraiser for a Hobe Sound man whose fiance died Monday in a house fire that destroyed the couple's belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a house fire that broke out at her home in Hobe Sound on Monday. Investigators with the sheriff's office believe an electrical issue may have caused the blaze, though the fire remains under investigation. The community has since come together to support White's fiancé Mark as he faces the devastating loss and the practical challenge of rebuilding after the flames destroyed much of their home and possessions.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the tragedy when Mark called to tell her the news. Fenn has been involved in efforts to help Mark move forward, including a fundraiser launched by friends to assist with rebuilding. When describing the state of the home after the fire, Fenn said it presented a completely devastating scene. She reflected on what made White special, noting that White was a Christian woman who had a passion for gardening and plants. White also played piano and was always ready to help others. Fenn emphasized that White loved children and people in general, and that she was known for being the first to offer assistance when someone needed it.

The loss carries additional weight for Mark, who has already experienced profound grief. According to Fenn, Mark lost his only child, Jacob, in a tragic circumstance. White's death compounds the heartbreak he has already endured. The timing of the tragedy makes the loss even more difficult for those close to them. White's birthday was July 4th, meaning she died just days before what would have been her birthday celebration.

Despite the devastating circumstances, those who knew White want her memory to live on. Fenn said White had always been a good soul and will remain in the hearts of those who loved her. The community's response through the fundraiser and support for Mark demonstrates how White's impact extended beyond her immediate family. As the investigation into the fire's cause continues, the focus for those close to White remains on honoring her memory and supporting Mark through this difficult period of loss and recovery.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for social media co.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended for social media comments about conservative commentator Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, stating "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

Last month, Judge Livingstone issued an order citing a Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no timeline set for a decision.

cards.headline: Juno Beach fence dispute over JB-7 beach access could cost town thousands
cards.teaser: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers are cutting through private property at the JB-7 public walkway since the town removed a fence in 2023.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now separating the public access path from private land, the problem intensifies during summer months. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, described cars parking in private spots and visitors cutting through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. She said residents previously confronted trespassers directly but now call police after confrontations became hostile.

The dispute reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official stated the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring a lower-cost solution, proposing a combination of split rail fencing and shrubs. Hill expressed hope that the town will reinstall the fence to restore their landscaping and private parking areas. The council agreed to address the fence question during its budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation to nearly double capacity
cards.teaser: The downtown public dock in Stuart will close July 6 for renovations projected to be complete by next Fourth of July, expanding from 18 to 44 slips.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. The project is projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. When finished, the dock will nearly double its capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve purposes beyond capacity expansion. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock to continue boarding passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said modernizing and expanding the dock will benefit both the city and local businesses.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to FDOT to help build a partial interchange on the Turnpike at Midway Road.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Samples stated the project is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth projected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial Turnpike interchange is also still in the design phase. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. The city council will vote on final approval of the land donation at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County to consider elevated self-driving transit from West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: A California company proposes an elevated network of autonomous vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would link the airport, convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations through small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers traveling along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center, potentially cutting the downtown-to-airport trip to less than 10 minutes.

The company describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers. Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin deeper discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing.

cards.headline: 15 DUI arrests made in St. Lucie County ahead of Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County deputies made 15 DUI arrests as part of efforts to target impaired driving before the Fourth of July holiday.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County deputies made 15 DUI arrests as part of a targeted enforcement effort to address impaired driving ahead of the Fourth of July holiday weekend. The arrests were made as deputies focused on removing impaired drivers from the roads during one of the busiest travel periods of the year.

The enforcement effort comes as hundreds of residents and visitors are expected to travel throughout St. Lucie County for holiday celebrations and gatherings. Law enforcement agencies across the Treasure Coast have increased patrols and checkpoints during the holiday weekend to prevent accidents and keep roads safe.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned national recognition as one of only 10 communities across the United States selected to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city stands as the sole Florida recipient of this year's honor. The prestigious award recognizes communities that unite residents, local government, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and create meaningful change. City leaders presented Riviera Beach's accomplishments at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where judges announced the city as a first-time winner. Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the recognition, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson emphasized that the city earned the award through sustained efforts to revitalize the community and enhance quality of life for residents, noting that people "are seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do."

The award reflects years of work focused on improving civic health, strengthening trust between residents and government, and enabling the community to actively shape the city's future. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents. Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another." She emphasized that the achievement belongs to the entire community and motivates continued progress. Miller-Anderson noted that winning the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride.

Several civic programs were highlighted in the city's award application, demonstrating the commitment to community engagement. The Riviera Beach Youth Council enables high school students to participate in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education program, achieved a 98% completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program offers mini-grants to longtime homeowners for critical property repairs. City leaders describe these initiatives as part of a broader commitment to treating civic engagement as an ongoing partnership between government, residents, faith groups, schools and community organizations. Miller-Anderson stated the city is "doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city."

The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and ranks among the nation's most respected civic honors. Officials say the designation celebrates Riviera Beach's progress while positioning the community for future opportunities and continued growth. Being named an All-America City communicates to the nation that Riviera Beach is a community where collaboration produces results and residents remain deeply engaged in shaping their city's direction.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie pushes forward on Midway Road widening and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to address accessibility and accommodate growth in the city over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange for the Turnpike is also still in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with comments on social media that labeled Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims the Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance in a deadly home fire earlier this week.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark, who stated that Misty had passed away in a fire. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said.

Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn reflected on White's character and how she wants her to be remembered. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. The timing adds another layer of heartbreak, as Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July, meaning she passed just a few days before her birthday.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for hundreds of Fourth of July boaters
cards.teaser: Hundreds of boaters are hitting the waterways across Florida to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend, and Martin County Maritime Response Unit is preparing for the crowds.
cards.body:
Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon were launching off the ramps on Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water as hundreds of boaters are hitting the waterways across Florida to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend.

Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said they're expecting hundreds of boaters on the water celebrating this weekend. His team will have two boats with medics on standby in Martin County in the north and south. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said. Harry said he wants boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: A recently diagnosed breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. After completing the mastectomy, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. According to the denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers investigational with insufficient proof that it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications. Despite the denial, Clark underwent the reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago with Billington's assistance. Anthem responded by stating it regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that without FDA approval, the mesh does not meet the standards required for coverage. Clark and Billington continue to fight the denial. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction after investigative reporting.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year across Florida
cards.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation as the culprit behind rising prices. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, the biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan," Woroch said.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state championship after 10-2 season and district title
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is working hard this summer with the goal of winning a state championship during the 2026 fall season. After finishing last year with a 10-2 record and claiming the district title, the team fell short in the second round of the playoffs. That early exit has motivated the Scots to push further in postseason play this year.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of his senior class, noting that most of them have been with the program since middle school. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. The experience and continuity within the leadership group is helping set higher expectations for the team moving forward.

To prepare for increased competition, the Scots have intentionally scheduled more challenging opponents for the fall. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind this approach. "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people," Williams said. The difficult schedule serves both as preparation for postseason play and as a way to draw attention to the program.

For the Scots, success is ultimately measured by playoff performance rather than regular season results. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that advancing beyond the second round is the team's primary goal. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean noted that the daily summer training sessions are building momentum and serving as motivation. "It just adds up every day as something like to look forward to. Work harder so we can see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record," St. Jean said. With experienced leadership and an intensive offseason program, the Scots are positioning themselves for a deeper run into the playoffs.

cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is placing two boats with medics on standby for the Fourth of July weekend as hundreds of boaters take to the waterways.

Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit the waterways across Florida this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.teaser: Friends are raising money to help a Hobe Sound man rebuild after his fiance, Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a home fire that destroyed their belongings.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach has been named one of 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders presented their efforts to strengthen community engagement. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the city's long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs: the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that the award is a tribute to their heart and determination. She added that winning the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday opposing an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Spectrum Academy teacher Matt Theobald with back pay.
cards.body:

The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027. The partial interchange is still in the design phase according to FDOT. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof repairs and lien removed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien lifted from his home and roof repairs completed after WPTV contacted the roofing contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. Starting January 10, McCoy called, texted and emailed the company requesting they return to complete the repairs, but received no response except for one email from a worker on February 5 saying the owner would call him. The owner never did.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then arrived warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien against McCoy's home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing owed them for materials furnished to the property. McCoy feared he would need to hire an attorney to resolve the matter. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the Seabreeze Roofing owner, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons, Gulfeagle Supply signed and notarized a final waiver of lien within an hour. The contractor also sent crews back to finish the two problem areas on McCoy's roof.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Fourth of July with Fireworks and America 250 Events Today
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Season Programs Through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational programs through September during peak sea turtle nesting season. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs include red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment.

The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups encourage beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Florida advances rules barring undocumented students from state colleges and adult education programs
hero.body:
Florida's State Board of Education voted to move forward with rules that would prevent undocumented students from enrolling in the state's 28 community colleges and adult education programs. The restrictions would also affect GED preparation courses, which many students use as a pathway to college or workforce training. This action follows a similar decision by Florida's public university system, which approved a plan to bar undocumented students starting in the 2027-28 academic year. Students already enrolled would not be affected by the university proposal.

Those backing the restrictions argue that taxpayer-funded educational institutions should prioritize students who are legally present in the United States. However, immigrant advocates and students have strongly opposed the changes. Alexander Vallejos, a student with DACA protections, argued that the rules would shut doors for young people raised in Florida who graduated from Florida schools. "We're just asking for an opportunity to earn our future through education," Vallejos said. "Because when Dreamers succeed, Florida succeeds." These new restrictions build on Florida's earlier decision to eliminate in-state tuition rates for many undocumented students, including those protected under DACA.

The education restrictions are part of a broader week of political activity in Florida under Governor Ron DeSantis. The governor moved to use a new state law, effective July 1, that allows the state to designate organizations as terrorist groups. DeSantis announced that Florida will seek to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the Muslim Brotherhood, and Antifa as terrorist organizations, along with more than 90 federally designated foreign terrorist organizations including cartel-connected groups and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. If approved by the Cabinet, these designations could cut off taxpayer funding, government contracts, and other public support to listed groups and create penalties for providing material support.

CAIR and civil rights organizations immediately filed lawsuits in federal court, arguing that the designations violate constitutional protections. Scott McCoy, deputy legal director for the Southern Poverty Law Center, stated that "Gov. DeSantis does not have the power to unilaterally brand an organization with this vilifying designation and punish those who support it without due process or judicial review." The lawsuit contends the designation process infringes on free speech and due process rights. DeSantis and supporters of the law maintain that the state is taking necessary steps to combat extremism and protect public institutions.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds raises $90 million as GOP governor's race heats up with ballot eligibility lawsuit
cards.teaser: U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds entered the week with more than $90 million raised this cycle as Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed a lawsuit challenging another candidate's ballot eligibility.
cards.body:
Byron Donalds and his affiliated political committee have raised more than $90 million this cycle, including more than $23 million in the second quarter. The campaign launched a $20 million statewide advertising buy as Florida's August primary draws closer. Donalds picked up endorsements from Attorney General James Uthmeier and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, both appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis, plus backing from incoming Senate President Jim Boyd and House Speaker Sam Garrison. DeSantis himself has not endorsed a successor in the race to replace him as he faces term limits, though several figures connected to his administration have begun lining up behind Donalds.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed a lawsuit arguing that Republican candidate James Fishback does not meet Florida's constitutional requirement that a governor live in the state for at least seven years before being elected. The legal complaint points to Fishback's ties to Washington, D.C., including allegations that he claimed a D.C. property as a primary residence and voted there in 2020. Fishback denied the allegations, arguing he was born and raised in Florida and accusing Collins of trying to damage his campaign. Fishback suggested without providing evidence that Collins is working in concert with Donalds. The court fight adds uncertainty to the GOP primary, with mail ballots going out soon and the Aug. 18 primary approaching.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lt. Gov. Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous social media accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts were deactivated after allegations tied them to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, with accusations coming from prominent veterans of Gov. Ron DeSantis' communications team.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, identified two X accounts they alleged were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to a known number and email used by Layla Collins. Screenshots verified this through two-factor authentication, displaying a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits visible.

Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. After Pushaw and Redfern publicly leveled these criticisms, both accounts were deactivated. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan for Tropicana Field redevelopment centered on civic park and museum
cards.teaser: The Burg Bid proposal, selected by Mayor Ken Welch, calls for transforming the Tropicana Field site into a mixed-use district organized around a 13-acre park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, The Burg Bid calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain. The proposal includes a $20 million deposit upon execution of a purchase and sale agreement. The $8.1 billion plan transforms stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district featuring housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, workforce training, public art and entertainment space. Unlike the previous redevelopment deal centered on a new stadium, The Burg Bid organizes around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central park that would include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad and a concert lawn. The park anchors 18.5 acres of total public park space on site.

The proposal includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg, plus homeownership opportunities at discounts to market value. The district would be built in three phases of approximately five years each, with early development beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The team's lease with the city ends after the 2028 season. Phase 1 would establish cultural and workforce anchors including the Woodson, the Collaboratorium workforce training center and a multimodal transportation hub.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd asks court to keep Paula Stark off ballot after incomplete qualifying paperwork
cards.teaser: Paula Stark's incomplete qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12, and state employees say crucial paperwork was never submitted.
cards.body:
In response to Paula Stark's Leon Circuit Court lawsuit, Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the courts to keep Stark off the ballot, casting doubt on her claims about a paperwork mix-up. Five state employees gave sworn written court declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the crucial Form 6 nor was he accidentally handed it back when he submitted remaining paperwork in the final 30 minutes before the June 12 noon qualifying deadline. Byrd argued in his response that had Stark or Davis exercised basic care by questioning why Form 6 was allegedly handed back, "the mistake would have been discovered" while Davis was at the Division. Three weeks after the deadline passed, Stark still had not submitted Form 6, according to Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve.

Form 6 is a public disclosure of financial interests. Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in Form 6, though half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve also criticized Stark's history of paperwork violations, noting Davis filed a campaign finance report over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark is not on the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 opens to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. Friends are raising money to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the fire destroyed their belongings.
hero.body:

Nina Fenn, who had known White for eight years, received the news through a phone call from Mark informing her that Misty had died in the fire. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn added. The loss carries additional weight for Mark, who had previously experienced profound tragedy. According to Fenn, he lost his only child, Jacob, in a past tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. "So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him."

The timing of White's death makes the loss even more painful for those who knew her. Her birthday was scheduled for July Fourth, just days after she died. Fenn reflected on how White's memory will remain with those who loved her. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said. Those grieving White's death are relying on their community for support during this difficult time.

According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains the final authority to decide whether Theobald returns to his position, with no timeline announced for a final decision.
